unmapped: Coactive/preference feedback: learner presents object y_t and receives an improved object bar y_t (no utility observed); this is not standard dueling feedback
Feedback is alpha-informative: U(x,bar y)-U(x,y) = alpha(U(x,y*)-U(x,y)) - xi_t with unknown alpha in (0,1] and slack xi_t >= 0
Linear utility U(x,y)=w*^T phi(x,y) with joint feature map ||phi(x,y)|| <= R; contexts x_t arbitrary
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, the learning algorithm receives a context $\bx_t \in {\cal X}$ and presents a (possibly structured) object $\by_t \in {\cal Y}$. In response, the user returns an object $\bby_t \in {\cal Y}$ which the algorithm receives as feedback. ... We say that user feedback is {\em $\alpha$-informative}, if for some $\alpha \in (0,1]$ and $\xi_t \ge 0$ ... $U(\bx,\by) = \bw^{*\top} \phi(\bx,\by)$ ... such that $\|\phi(\bx,\by)\| \le R$

symbols.alpha_inf: informativeness parameter alpha in (0,1] of the user feedback
symbols.w_norm: ||w*||, Euclidean norm of the unknown utility parameter

conditions: user feedback is alpha-informative with slacks xi_t >= 0

source.label: thm:bound
source.quote: Under $\alpha$-informative feedback the algorithm in Figure \ref{perceptron} has regret \text{REGRET}_T \le \frac{1}{\alpha T} \! \sum_{t=1}^T \xi_t + \frac{2R \|\bw^* \|}{ \alpha \sqrt{T}}.

results.notes: Paper's REGRET_T is average regret; multiplied by T. Bound is deterministic (holds for every sequence). R mapped to L_feat. Setting mapping (dueling feedback, linear_infinite) is approximate.
